channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Results from the 2026 State of CSS Survey
Josh Comeau wrote an excellent primer on anchor positioning
item.description: For decades, one of the most notoriously-challenging problems on the web has been sticking one element to another element, for things like tooltips and nested menus. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Styling the Navigation: Declarative Route and Navigation Matching in CSS
item.description: One of the things that we at Chrome have been thinking about for a while now is a way to do declarative route and navigation matching in CSS. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Gap Decorations Are Now Available, Here's What's New
item.description: Today, with CSS gap decorations fully supported in Chrome and Edge, starting with version 149, you can now very easily style gaps, and with a lot of control. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Microsoft Edge is about to lock out older ad blockers, just like Chrome did
item.description: Microsoft Edge is ending support for Manifest V2 extensions like uBlock Origin starting this month. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: IP and DNS Leaks in WebKit Affecting Proxy Browsers and iCloud Private Relay
item.description: WebKit-based browsers on iOS and macOS can be configured to route all web traffic through proxy servers, which is how Tor browsers on iOS and our own Psylo work. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Kitesurf: Agent-first browser that runs in V8 isolates
item.description: We should be giving all agents tools that excel at what’s important for an AI model. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: MDN shares its pageview data
item.description: TIL: MDN exposes up-to-date page view data through https://popularities.mdn.mozilla.net/current.csv. Using Google AI Studio, I generated a visualizer to explore the data. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Uno Platform 6.6 Adds Native AOT, Vulkan Rendering, and Broader Accessibility Support
item.description: Uno Platform 6.6 introduces Native AOT publishing across five target platforms, an optional Vulkan rendering backend, and automatic registration for the framework’s Model Context Protocol servers. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Get Screenshots of Your Frontend in Each PR
item.description: Greptile TREX runs your PR branch in a sandbox to catch the bugs that only show up at runtime, then leaves the logs, screenshots, and traces on the PR. (1 source: frontendfocus)
